title: Which of 3375 and 500 is a perfect cube?
description: Two numbers are tested by splitting their prime factors into three equal groups, and the cube root is read from one group. Keeko doubts five hundred, because it has three fives.
teaching_notes: One idea: a perfect cube splits into three equal groups of prime factors. Watch for students who see one factor repeated three times and ignore the other factors.

source: Decide whether 3375 and 500 are perfect cubes, and give the cube root of the one that is.
video_script.why: The child tests whether a number is a perfect cube by splitting its prime factors into three equal groups, and reads the cube root from one group.
video_script.substitution: Break the number into prime factors, try to form three equal groups, and multiply one group to get the cube root.
video_script.anchor: two number cards, three thousand three hundred seventy five and five hundred
video_script.wrong_answer: five hundred has three fives, so it is a perfect cube
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees three fives in five hundred and calls it a perfect cube. Every prime factor must come in groups of three, and the two twos are left over.
video_script.payoff_line: Three thousand three hundred seventy five is fifteen cubed, with cube root fifteen

final_answer.value: 3375 = 15³, cube root 15; 500 is not a perfect cube
final_answer.spoken: three thousand three hundred seventy five is fifteen cubed, with cube root fifteen, and five hundred is not a perfect cube

hold_back: 3375 = 15³, cube root 15; 500 is not a perfect cube
maths_rules: 500 = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 5; two 2s cannot make three equal groups
video_script.design: One idea: three equal groups of prime factors. Wrong idea: three of one factor is enough. The two cards stay in the anchor band and the factor lines sit on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step one, break three thousand three hundred seventy five into prime factors.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Dividing by three, three times, leaves one hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='five'/>That is five times five times five, so we get three threes and three fives.

narration: <bookmark mark='group'/>Step two, split the factors into three equal groups. Each group is three times five, which is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='cubed'/>That makes three thousand three hundred seventy five equal to fifteen times fifteen times fifteen.
<bookmark mark='triplet'/>Another way is to group the equal factors in triplets, three cubed times five cubed.
<bookmark mark='root'/>Either way, the cube root is fifteen.

beats.on_screen: 500 = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 5; only two 2s, so no three equal groups

marks.short: the two 2s are circled and cannot fill three groups

narration: <bookmark mark='fac'/>Step three, break five hundred into prime factors.
It is two times two times five times five times five.
<bookmark mark='short'/>There are only two twos, so the factors cannot make three equal groups.
<bookmark mark='no'/>Five hundred is not a perfect cube.

marks.back: the words put the answer back in the question are written

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Fifteen times fifteen is two hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Two hundred twenty five times fifteen is three thousand three hundred seventy five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 3375 = 15³, cube root 15; 500 is not a perfect cube
